question: Does contact identity/repeatability and response to the frozen governor differ for a low ridge below nominal bracket clearance versus the existing 22mm ridge?

obstacle.qualification: Geometry contrast is a new declared scenario, not a correction or replacement of the 22mm failures. 6mm was chosen below the 9.03mm nominal bracket gap, not as a claimed safe hardware height.

logging: all arrivals, failures and 2s post-arrival stop checks
first named manifold and first positive-depth nonzero-force sample separately
wheel/caster identity, precontact support/load and rolling state for diagnostics only
raw command/encoder/GT/IMU timestamps, native replay and coverage
unchanged whole-route and post-contact vibration/slip, time and physical tracking
stop_rule: Stop on missing measurement or physical failure; retain all attempts and do not run replacements. At budget end, inspect mechanism and repeatability, do not select the easier height to claim general improvement.
interpretation: n=2 per arm/height is a mechanism screen only. A change of first-contact component with height supports a scope distinction, not proof of mechanical fault. Stable quality benefit would justify a separately budgeted confirmation; mixed effects mean offline audit and a go/no-go decision, not automatic tuning.
